figures.description: Information Required for Construction of Drilled Shafts Site investigation scoping; bid document preparation; constructability review Most frequently cited cause of drilled shaft failure: improper construction Artesian conditions and high seepage must be clearly indicated on boring logs For rock-bearing shafts: pre-construction coring to verify no 'floater' and evaluate rock quality Establish rock quality criteria and payment provisions for additional excavation before construction Technique shaft (trial shaft) during design phase reveals constructability issues not seen in borings All constructability information must be disclosed to bidders

figures.description: Recommended Minimum Scope for Geotechnical Investigations Site investigation program scoping; boring program design AASHTO minimum: 1 boring per substructure ≤100 ft wide, ≥2 for wider substructures For drilled shafts: bore at every shaft location when rock-bearing, especially in variable conditions Rock core minimum: 10 ft or 3× shaft diameter (isolated) or 2× group dimension, whichever greater Probe holes during construction for highly variable bedrock instead of more pre-construction borings Phased investigations appropriate; align investigation scope with project design stage
